answers.question: Can I do all three runs next week and add the two I missed?
answers.answer: No, the plan does not add the two missed runs and it does not add a third run this week. Next week has two short run-walks, Wednesday and Saturday, and each one only if you have no fever and your breathing feels normal. If either day feels harder than you expect, swap it for a walk. The missed sessions are gone, and adding them would mean five runs in one week while you are still recovering.

new.analysis:
## What you followed
Your Monday run-walk was the only session that happened, and it matched the plan at 2.78 km. Your average heart rate was 139 with a peak of 146, which is a comfortable effort for you. You also took your rest days, so nothing was overrun during the week.

## What was skipped and why it matters
Wednesday and Saturday were skipped after a cold turned into a fever on Wednesday night. That was the right decision, because running through a fever adds risk for little gain. Those two sessions are gone, and making them up now would work against your recovery.

## Why next week is light
You are still coughing and congested, and you say you feel wiped out. Adding the two missed runs on top of the usual three would mean five runs in one week while you are still getting over a fever. Two easy run-walks with rest days between them keep your routine going without asking for more than you have.

## Why no hard work yet
The build phase adds threshold work, but that comes after several clear weeks of steady running. Starting harder efforts while you are still recovering would be a mistake. The first goal is to get back to three clean runs a week, and then one quality session can be added.

## The race
The Corrowmore Harvest 5K is about two months away, which is enough time to go from run-walking to running the whole way if the build is steady. Your Monday intervals ran at about 7:40/km with heart rate staying well under your ceiling, so the fitness is there. Once you feel fully well, return to your usual Monday, Wednesday and Saturday routine, and keep most runs easy.
